formula_checks.name: buildBudgetState
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Missing stored expenses become zero and therefore produce a positive projected saving without a budget.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Refuse projected saving until income and budget completeness are known.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: spend = doc.monthly_spending || 0. Its only caller, budgetFromOnboarding, hands plannedMonthlySpend, which is 0 when nothing is set — so "no budget" and "a confirmed $0" both give projected_to_save = the whole take-home.
formula_checks.plain_example: $5,000 take-home, no budget set: projected saving $5,000; right: no figure ("not set").
formula_checks.production_callers: MK-XS-F-031 buildSnapshot (HomeScreen) → goal capacity (when no monthlySavingsCapacity is typed) and retire_monthly_spend_today; Home reads only snapshot.networth, so no screen prints it today.
formula_checks.note: The income it subtracts from is buildIncomeState's net_monthly_income — the legacy reader MK-CF-F-049 (part 5).
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-BUDGET): buildBudgetState refuses (null) when no budget is set; budgetFromOnboarding stores no plan when nothing was entered (DEC-7939, tenet 3).

formula_checks.name: expenses
formula_checks.reviewer_why: The approved drawing and formula can reconcile expenses, but linked-card payment exclusion differs from the actual flow contract, and repeated names can double-assign a payment.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Use stable debt identity and one stated treatment for card purchases versus balance payments, preserving section totals.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: (a) Name matching gives one logged payment to every debt with the same normalized name (via F-150), so the Expenses tab's actual total counts it twice while This month's actual (F-157 debtPaymentsByDebt, a name→id map) counts it once against the last such debt. (b) The linked-card exclusion exists only in expenses/radar; actualMonthFlow has none — but no production caller marks a card captured (theMonth passes the default empty set), so the two agree today. The card should say so.
formula_checks.plain_example: Debts "Loan" and " loan ", one $250 payment: Expenses actual $500, This month actual $250.
formula_checks.production_callers: MK-CF-O-010 theMonth (CashFlowScreen Expenses tab and This month; HomeScreen via useThisMonthInputs).
formula_checks.note: The approved frame C household reconciles exactly ($2,250 / $2,000 / $2,100).
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-MONTH): FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-MONTH): one matcher, debtPaymentsMatched (logged-expenses.ts) — a payment goes to the debt whose id it names ("Log a payment" now writes debtId, BudgetScreen.tsx and MoneySheets.tsx), else to the one debt with its payee's name; a name two debts share is given to neither and listed once ("Other debt payments · logged as “Loan” — two of your debts have that name, so it is given to neither"; on Expenses "Loan payment $250 · two of your debts have that name — counted once").

formula_checks.name: debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Name-based payment matching can attach one expense to multiple debts with identical normalized names.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Require stable debt identity or flag ambiguous matches; a logged amount may be counted once.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: For each non-instalment debt it adds every Debt payment log whose payee equals the debt's label (trim, lower case). Two debts with one normalized name each receive the whole payment. Production stores no debt id on a payment (store = d.label in BudgetScreen.tsx and MoneySheets.tsx) and no screen stops duplicate debt names.
formula_checks.plain_example: "Loan" + " loan ", $250 logged: Loan payment $250 and " loan  payment" $250.
formula_checks.note: MK-CF-F-153 radar uses the same match and lists both; MK-CF-F-157 debtPaymentsByDebt (part 14) gives it to one debt only. One fix should give all three one debt-identity rule.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-MONTH): FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-MONTH): one matcher, debtPaymentsMatched (logged-expenses.ts) — a payment goes to the debt whose id it names ("Log a payment" now writes debtId, BudgetScreen.tsx and MoneySheets.tsx), else to the one debt with its payee's name; a name two debts share is given to neither and listed once ("Other debt payments · logged as “Loan” — two of your debts have that name, so it is given to neither"; on Expenses "Loan payment $250 · two of your debts have that name — counted once").

formula_checks.name: radar
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Known debt due/paid selection is coherent, but the prose does not establish the date window of bigBills or prevent showing a future bill as this month’s expense.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Declare bigBills input scope and filter dated bills to the queried month; do not treat a radar forecast as paid.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: radar lists every bigBills entry of $500 or more it is handed; the entry has a due label and no date, so filtering to the month is the caller's job. No production caller hands bigBills (thisMonthInputs builds none), so no future bill can reach this month's radar — and no non-debt bill reaches it at all. The radar never deducts (theMonth's planned surplus is the same with or without it).
formula_checks.plain_example: October, a $1,200 December insurance bill: through the real door the radar is empty.
formula_checks.note: The reviewer's point is a gap in the card's words, not a wrong number: the card should say the caller hands the month's bills and that today none is handed. Whether a large once-in-a-while bill should show on its month's radar is raised as a ruling item.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-MONTH): the door hands the month's dated bills; the rule text says so.

formula_checks.name: theBudgetCounted
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Suppresses the named home mortgage category correctly, but does not identify any other debt duplicated in a user budget despite the broader any-debt rule.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Keep the home rule; require explicit debt links/exclusions for other duplicated debt categories and disclose any unresolved duplicates.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Only the budget's Rent / Mortgage line (id rent) stands down, and only for the home's mortgage. The budget editor also offers a "Debt payment" category (BUDGET_CATEGORIES id debt) and custom lines; either, holding a debt that is also in Debts, is counted twice in the planned outflow.
formula_checks.plain_example: $250 car loan in Debts + a $250 budget line for it: planned outflow $500; right $250.
formula_checks.production_callers: useCashflowModel, useThisMonthInputs, CashFlowScreen, BillCalendarScreen, MK-NW-O-004 theEmergencyFund.
formula_checks.note: The home-mortgage rule itself agrees in all four drawn cases.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-MONTH): every budget line that is a debt in Debts stands down; a mortgage on no property beside a Rent / Mortgage line is that line (the lead's ruling) — counted once, planned and actual (expensesAsCounted).

needs_a_ruling.item: Does the big-ticket radar show a large once-in-a-while bill in its own month?

needs_a_ruling.reading_b: Keep the radar to card, credit-line and lump-sum debts only, and drop "or a bill well above its usual size" from its empty-state sentence (drawing frame D).
needs_a_ruling.example: $1,200 car insurance due December: today it is on no month's radar; the drawing's empty radar says a bill well above its usual size would appear.
needs_a_ruling.recommendation: Reading A — the drawing's own sentence promises it, DEC-0002 gives big one-off bills their own list, and the month filter comes free from the plan's dated cell.

The month table hands each month its dated bills (datedBillsIn, src/domain/grid — FIX-BILLS, 2026-10-25); feeding the radar from it is FIX-MONTH's (expenses.ts, thisMonthInputs).
